title: Use threat modeling to improve a design before it fails: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which model elements and method expose the plausible abuse path, and what decision must result?
focalInsight: Bound the system with assets, actors, flows, and trust boundaries; choose methods for the question; own treatment.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Threat Modeling
nodes.definition: Bounded attacker/failure analysis of a system.
nodes.detail: Bounded attacker/failure analysis of a system.
nodes.decision: Set scope, asset, actor, flow, method, owner.

altSummary: Bound the system with assets, actors, flows, and trust boundaries; choose methods for the question; own treatment.
textFallback:
threat modeling: Bounded attacker/failure analysis of a system. Decide: Set scope, asset, actor, flow, method, owner. Example/failure: Attack list has no system model. Retrieve: It changes design decisions.
assets: Valuable data, service, credential, trust relationship. Decide: Identify protection target and consequence. Example/failure: Admin credential omitted. Retrieve: Assets anchor priority.
actors: People/services/attackers interacting with system. Decide: Name authority, entry, legitimate/malicious roles. Example/failure: Partner admin omitted. Retrieve: Actors expose identity assumptions.
trust boundary: Where authority/trust/control changes. Decide: Mark crossing and require validation/authorization. Example/failure: External input becomes trusted internally. Retrieve: Boundaries need controls.
data flow: Path of data/commands between components. Decide: Map source, destination, content, protocol, store. Example/failure: Queue/backup path omitted. Retrieve: Flows show exposure.
attack surface: Influenceable interfaces, inputs, identities, dependencies. Decide: Prioritize exposed/privileged expansion. Example/failure: Webhook adds commands unreviewed. Retrieve: Surface is more than ports.
threat: Plausible adverse action against asset/path. Decide: Use method after system context. Example/failure: SQL injection listed without input target. Retrieve: Tie threat to asset/path/consequence.
mitigation: Design/control/test reducing modeled threat. Decide: Assign owner, acceptance, proof, residual risk. Example/failure: Validation proposed but untested. Retrieve: Mitigation needs evidence.
abuse case: Narrative of harmful misuse of intended path. Decide: Test business logic/authorization. Example/failure: Refund repeats approvals. Retrieve: It finds feature misuse.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: Which model elements and method expose the plausible abuse path, and what decision must result?
learningContract.misconception: A named methodology or a generic attack list is a complete threat model.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned rows expose distinctions, decision criteria, and misuse consequences.
learningContract.focalInsight: Bound the system with assets, actors, flows, and trust boundaries; choose methods for the question; own treatment.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Implementation settings and jurisdiction-specific conclusions are not inferred from these concise concept comparisons.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: Map a boundary and choose STRIDE, LINDDUN, OCTAVE, or another method with a reason.
